patients.summary: HR coordinator who joined mid-way through her second pregnancy, then delivered at 32 weeks by emergent repeat cesarean for fetal distress; her son had a NICU course with IVH and anemia of prematurity. Quiet primary-care years followed until a 2026 complete hydatidiform mole with severe preeclampsia, evacuated by suction curettage, now under gynecology hCG surveillance.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 yo here to set up primary care. Currently pregnant, about 21 weeks by LMP (~1/22/23), seeing an outside OB group for prenatal care; she says everything has gone smoothly so far. No bleeding, no leaking, no headaches or vision change.

OB hx: this is her second pregnancy. First was in 2021, carried to term, delivered by low transverse C-section, healthy baby.

PMH: nothing chronic. PSH: C-section as above.
Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, started by her OB this pregnancy.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: her mother had preeclampsia with a pregnancy. A maternal aunt was treated for gestational trophoblastic disease.
SH: works in HR as a coordinator. Never smoker. Drinks rarely, a drink or two a month before pregnancy, none now.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well, gravid. Ht 165 cm. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen gravid, low transverse scar well healed. No leg swelling. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Pregnancy, ~21 wks, followed by OB. Uncomplicated so far. We will stay out of the prenatal lane; she knows to call OB first for anything pregnancy-related. Asked her to have OB copy us on major notes.
2. Health maintenance: will get records from her old primary office (form signed). Vaccines in pregnancy per OB, she expects Tdap there in the third trimester.
3. Iron per OB, continue.

RTC after delivery or sooner as needed.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

conditions.label: Acute fetal distress requiring emergent delivery

documents.title: Baby came early
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to let you know the baby came Sunday at 32 weeks. My water broke early that morning and his heart rate kept dropping on the monitor so they did an emergency C-section. I'm sore but ok. He's in the NICU. Yesterday the nurses saw him turn blue a few times while he was sleeping, maybe 20 seconds each, he goes floppy and then comes back on his own. They say his oxygen is fine in between and it's not with feeding. They're watching him closely. Not really sure what I'm asking, I guess just keeping you in the loop. I'm still in the hospital until Thursday.

documents.title: Re: Baby came early
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Susan, thank you for letting me know, and congratulations on your son. That's a lot to happen in one weekend. The NICU team is the right place for him and they will walk you through what they're seeing. For you: rest, take the pain medicine the OB team sends you home with, and call your OB for fever, heavy bleeding or wound redness. I'd like to see you in about a month to check in on how you're recovering. Front desk will reach out. Thinking of you all.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY (outside hospital)
Admitted 09/10/2023, discharged 09/14/2023.

G2P1 at 32 weeks with a prior low transverse cesarean presented with a sudden gush of clear fluid and irregular contractions roughly every 10 minutes. No bleeding, no significant pain. Prenatal course uncomplicated with adequate care. Vitals stable on arrival. Sterile speculum exam confirmed ROM; cervix 3 cm, vertex. Continuous monitoring showed abrupt decelerations from a baseline of 140 to 90 bpm with quick recovery, variable in relation to contractions. Given recurrent decelerations, proceeded to emergent repeat low transverse cesarean for fetal distress. Liveborn male, admitted to NICU.

Postoperative course unremarkable; incision clean and dry at discharge, ambulating, tolerating diet.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily (continue).
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit; routine wound care.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary reviewed. Preterm ROM at 32 wks, decels, emergent repeat LTCS. Follow up postpartum next month.

documents.title: Update and appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. Update on the baby since you asked. He's still on CPAP for his breathing (respiratory distress syndrome they call it) and yesterday he had more spells where he stops breathing and his heart rate drops. They did a head ultrasound and found a bleed in his brain, an intraventricular hemorrhage. His soft spot was a little sunken. They said no seizures and his neuro exam was ok. He also has anemia of prematurity. His scores at birth were 8 and 9 so they were hopeful at first. It's a lot. Could I move my appointment with you to later in the month? I'm at the NICU most days.

documents.title: Re: Update and appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Susan. I'm sorry this has been so hard. Of course we can move it. The front desk will offer you 10/17, first slot of the morning so you can get to the NICU after. Please reach out sooner if you're not sleeping, not eating, or feeling hopeless, any time.

documents.title: Appointment rescheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Moved f/u to 10/17 at 8:00 per Dr. Pt confirmed.

conditions.label: History of preterm birth (32 weeks gestation)
Acute fetal distress requiring emergent delivery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Five weeks out from emergent repeat C-section at 32 wks (9/10). Incision sore early on, now barely notices it. Bleeding tapered to spotting. Son still inpatient: on CPAP, had apnea/bradycardia spells, head US showed an IVH, and he has anemia of prematurity. She is at the NICU most days. Sleeping in pieces. Feels anxious and teary at times, mostly around his ups and downs; no thoughts of self-harm. Eating ok. Has her OB postpartum visit at the end of the month.
Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 daily.

O: Looks tired but engaged, good eye contact. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, LTCS incision healed, no erythema or drainage. No calf tenderness or leg swelling. PHQ-9: 8.

A/P
1. S/p preterm delivery at 32 wks for fetal distress. Recovering well. Added history of preterm birth to her list; fetal distress problem closed.
2. Mood: PHQ-9 8 with a lot of situational strain. Not depression by history at this point. Talked about the NICU social worker and parent support group, sleep in shifts where she can. Told her to message me if it gets heavier; will re-screen at the next visit.
3. Iron: on ferrous sulfate. CBC today.
4. Flu and updated COVID given today.

RTC for physical in the spring.

documents.title: CBC result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Susan, your blood count from yesterday is normal, no anemia. Keep doing what you're doing. Hope the week is going ok.
